context.title: Micaiah and Ahab's Death
context.summary: Ahab and Jehoshaphat of Judah plan war on Ramoth-gilead. Four hundred prophets promise victory, but Micaiah foresees defeat. Ahab goes in disguise and is killed by a random arrow.
context.background: Ramoth-gilead was a fortified town east of the Jordan, contested between Israel and Syria. Jehoshaphat's alliance with Ahab was sealed by a marriage between their families (2 Kings 8:18). The chapter ends with brief notes on Jehoshaphat's reign and the start of Ahaziah's.

customs.note: Zedekiah acts out goring like a bull — a dramatic sign meant to guarantee victory.
Kings were often called shepherds; scattered sheep pictured a people whose king had fallen.

watchFor: Micaiah's vision of the LORD's heavenly council (vv. 19–23).
The arrow drawn 'at a venture' — by chance, yet fulfilling the word (vv. 34, 38).

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Jehoshaphat
people.summary: The son and successor of Asa, king of Judah. After fortifying his kingdom against Israel (2 Chr. 17:1, 2), he set himself to cleanse the land of idolatry (1 Kings 22:43).

people.name: Micaiah
people.summary: Who is like Jehovah?, the son of Imlah, a faithful prophet of Samaria (1 Kings 22:8-28). Three years after the great battle with Ben-hadad (20:29-34), Ahab proposed to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, that they should go up against Ramoth-Gilead to do battle again with Ben-hadad.

people.name: Imla
people.summary: Replenisher, the father of Micaiah the prophet (2 Chr. 18:7, 8).

people.name: Zedekiah
people.summary: The son of Chenaanah, a false prophet in the days of Ahab (1 Kings 22:11, 24; 2 Chr. 18:10, 23).

people.name: Ahab
people.summary: The son of Omri, whom he succeeded as the seventh king of Israel. His history is recorded in 1 Kings 16-22. His wife was Jezebel, who exercised a very evil influence over him.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Amon
people.summary: The governor of Samaria in the time of Ahab.

people.name: Joash
people.summary: One of King Ahab’s sons (1 Kings 22:26).

people.name: Ahaziah
people.summary: The son and successor of Ahab. He followed the counsels of his mother Jezebel, and imitated in wickedness the ways of his father. In his reign the Moabites revolted from under his authority (2 Kings 3:5-7).

people.name: Asa
people.summary: Physician, son of Abijah and grandson of Rehoboam, was the third king of Judah. He was zealous in maintaining the true worship of God, and in rooting all idolatry, with its accompanying immoralities, out of the land (1 Kings 15:8-14).

people.name: Azubah
people.summary: The daughter of Shilhi, and mother of king Jehoshaphat (1 Kings 22:42).

people.name: Esau
people.summary: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Jehoram
people.summary: The eldest son and successor of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah. He reigned eight years (B.C. 892-885) alone as king of Judah, having been previously for some years associated with his father (2 Chr. 21:5, 20; 2 Kings 8:16).

people.name: Jeroboam
people.summary: The son of Nebat (1 Kings 11:26-39), “an Ephrathite,” the first king of the ten tribes, over whom he reigned twenty-two years (B.C. 976-945).

people.name: Nebat
people.summary: Sight; aspect, the father of Jeroboam, the king of Israel (1 Kings 11:26, etc.).

people.name: Baal
people.summary: The name appropriated to the principal male god of the Phoenicians. It is found in several places in the plural BAALIM (Judg. 2:11; 10:10; 1 Kings 18:18; Jer. 2:23; Hos. 2:17).

places.name: Syria
places.summary: (Heb. Aram), the name in the Old Testament given to the whole country which lay to the north-east of Phoenicia, extending to beyond the Euphrates and the Tigris.

places.name: Ramoth-gilead
places.summary: Heights of Gilead, a city of refuge on the east of Jordan; called “Ramoth in Gilead” (Deut. 4:43; Josh. 20:8; 21:38). Here Ahab, who joined Jehoshaphat in an endeavour to rescue it from the hands of the king of Syria, was mortally wounded (1 Kings 22:1-36).

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: A watch-mountain or a watch-tower. In the heart of the mountains of Israel, a few miles north-west of Shechem, stands the “hill of Shomeron,” a solitary mountain, a great “mamelon.”

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Edom
places.summary: Idumea (Isa. 34:5, 6; Ezek. 35:15). “The field of Edom” (Gen. 32:3), “the land of Edom” (Gen. 36:16), was mountainous (Obad. 1:8, 9, 19, 21).

places.name: Ezion-geber
places.summary: The giant’s backbone (so called from the head of a mountain which runs out into the sea), an ancient city and harbour at the north-east end of the Elanitic branch of the Red Sea, the Gulf of Akabah, near Elath or Eloth (Num. 33:35; Deut. 2:8).

places.name: Ophir
places.summary: Some region famous for its gold (1 Kings 9:28; 10:11; 22:48; Job 22:24; 28:16; Isa. 13:12). In the LXX. this word is rendered “Sophir,” and “Sofir” is the Coptic name for India, which is the rendering of the Arabic version, as also of the Vulgate.

places.name: Tarshish
places.summary: The name of a place which first comes into notice in the days of Solomon. The question as to the locality of Tarshish has given rise to not a little discussion.

events.title: Reign of Jehoshaphat
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 22:41–50. People: Jehoshaphat. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 25 years.

events.title: Death of Jehoshaphat
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 22:50. People: Jehoshaphat. Place: Jerusalem.

events.title: Reign of Ahaziah
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 22:51–53. People: Ahaziah. Place: Samaria. Lasted about 2 years.
